source.name: archives.yotsubasociety.org (4chan Archived Threads)
source.short-desc: The Yotsuba Society Archives, which held publicly viewable 4chan thread archives, handmade by Jkid. Includes the Moot Video Archive as a bonus. This was obtained from RebeccaBlackTech from an unknown source, possibly direct web scrape.
source.capture: 23,295 thread pages across 63 board directories, laid out <board>/<threadno>.htm[l] with a sibling <threadno>_files/ of assets. Sampling says ~85% is the classic Futaba markup fybertech-html reads and ~14% is 4chan's own markup chan-html reads, so both adapters run over this same tree and each skips the other's pages -- see archives-yotsubasociety-org-native. A little of it is futaba/2chan (Japanese, class=del/chui) which is not 4chan at all and parses as nothing. ingest.path points at out/4chan deliberately: the mirror's root also holds 1chan, 4chon, auschan, bun and kuvalauta, which must not be ingested under site=4chan. Some filenames carry a human annotation ('1000000 ban.html', "b's reponse to question.htm") since the archive was handmade. THE UPSTREAM TARBALL IS TRUNCATED. All 17,602,887,852 bytes download and the md5 matches archive.org, so `download` reports success -- but the bytes themselves are broken: `gzip -t` fails with 'invalid compressed data--format violated' on the NAS as well as locally, which means archive.org is hosting a corrupt file rather than the transfer being at fault. About 22.7GB and 1,274,677 tar entries read out before it dies, so most of the site is recoverable; the prepare step deliberately ignores tar's exit code and keeps whatever extracted. Treat coverage as partial and unknown-at-the-tail. THE BOARD DIRECTORIES ARE NOT RELIABLE, which matters because the nested layout gives the adapter no other signal: 530 of the 23,295 pages sit in a directory that the page's own links contradict. THE BOARD IS DERIVED FROM THE PAGE'S LINKS, NOT ITS <title> -- a <form action="//sys.4chan.org/sp/post"> is where the page posts to, which a display name cannot change and a thread subject cannot fake. Measured over the whole mirror: link evidence exists for 99.4% of pages against 91.9% for titles, the two agree 99.5% of the time where both exist, and among the 530 genuine misfilings the title agreed with the links 501 times and with the directory 0 times. Some are simply misfiled (47 /tv/ threads under r9k/, a /b/ thread whose post number is 366,819,824 and so inflates r9k's apparent post_no range 4x), and 133 are the same thread filed under TWO board directories -- which ingests twice, once per board label, the one duplication UNIQUE (site, board, post_no) cannot catch because board is part of the key. The prepare pipeline now runs `reconcile-boards` to sort this out before ingest sees it; do not remove that step. Titles that name a different board than the links do are REPORTED AND NEVER ACTED ON, because every one found so far is a display-name costume over a correctly-filed board rather than a board missing from 4chan-board-lifespans.json: 746 pages titled /ɐ/ (April Fools upside-down /a/), 9 titled /g9k/ (April Fools /r9k/), 40 under vp/ titled /tr/ - Team Rocket, 1 under r9k/ titled /cwc/, 2 under test/ titled /adv/, and 49 under sp/ titled /wc/ with three rotating names (English Goalkeeping, Malian Refereeing, DEUTSCHLAND). Watch that report: an unfamiliar pair in it is the cue to investigate, and it is how /wc/ was caught. Hand-archivers also name files after general-thread abbreviations (/dpt/ daily programming thread, /bmg/ boymoder general), which look exactly like board tags and are not. /wc/ IS NOT AND NEVER WAS A BOARD -- it is /sp/ renamed for the 2010 World Cup, which is why no archive site or the Bibanon wiki mentions it. Evidence, checked in the pages themselves: all 2,324 internal links point at boards.4chan.org/sp/ and none at /wc/; the nav bar lists no /wc/; every post falls in 2010-06-13..2010-07-11 (the tournament ran Jun 11 - Jul 11) and the names track its controversies (Robert Green's fumble, Koman Coulibaly's disallowed goal); and the 43 numerically-named threads form one unbroken run of /sp/'s counter, 5,375,744..6,475,904, with plain /sp/ pages immediately below (5,350,269) and above (6,609,911). Six more are hand-named board-index saves ('_wc_ - DEUTSCHLAND.htm'). DO NOT ADD /wc/, /g9k/ OR /tr/ TO THE TIMELINE to make the report line go away: they are display names, and the timeline is a list of boards. An earlier version of this step took a 'foreign' list of board tags to quarantine as another imageboard's, matched against the <title>, and listed /tr/ and /cwc/; that was wrong and would have dropped 41 real 4chan pages (40 /vp/, 1 /r9k/) out of the ingest. The step excludes nothing -- it only moves files -- and it needs no help here. SEVEN DIRECTORIES ARE HAND-NAMED COLLECTIONS RATHER THAN BOARDS (4chanspecialcollection, GM, bay of pigs, board announcements, conventions, law and order hack, other) and THIS RESOLVES ITSELF: 179 of the 195 pages in them are real threads and get relocated to the board their links name -- 124 conventions -> con, 15 law and order hack (b:9 tv:4 g:1 a:1), 14 GM (a:7 r9k:2 b:2 cgl:1 lit:1 int:1), 14 bay of pigs spread over twelve boards, 7 4chanspecialcollection -> b, 3 board announcements, 2 other. The 16 that remain are not threads at all: six Apache 'Index of /4chan/<dir>' listings, and ten 4chan.net pages in 4chanspecialcollection (rules, FAQ, tripcodes, japanese, index2, the old banned page, a 'BRB!' holding page, an eBay listing for a 2006 Otakon box, the moot video archive). NO ingest.exclude-boards IS NEEDED and none is set: not one of the 16 contains class="reply", class="postername" or postContainer, so fybertech-html and chan-html both recognise nothing in them and store zero rows. Checked directly, not assumed.
